overviewTitle: Advanced Physics: Optics & Related Concepts (2-Week Curriculum)
introduction: This curriculum builds upon prior knowledge of waves, harmonics, and energy. It emphasizes the wave-particle duality of light and connects optics to upcoming topics in electrostatics and electrical currents.

topics.topicName: Review & Linkup: Waves, Harmonics, and Energy (Einstein)
keyPoints: Recap of wave properties: wavelength, frequency, amplitude, speed.
Harmonic motion and energy transfer.
Einstein's equation (E=mc²) and its connection to energy and mass.
Light as a form of energy – qualitative discussion of the electromagnetic spectrum.
topics.importance: Sets the stage for understanding light as both a wave and a particle, and connects to prior knowledge.

keyPoints: Nature of electromagnetic waves: oscillating electric and magnetic fields.
Relationship between electric and magnetic fields.
Qualitative discussion of the electromagnetic spectrum (radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma).
Applications: radio communication, microwaves in cooking, medical imaging (X-rays).
topics.importance: Introduces the concept of EM waves and their diverse applications, bridging waves and optics.

subtopics.name: Reflection and Refraction
keyPoints: Law of reflection.
Snell's Law (qualitative discussion, focusing on bending of light).
Total internal reflection (qualitative explanation).
subtopics.importance: Foundation for understanding image formation and lens behavior.

subtopics.name: Lenses
keyPoints: Types of lenses (convex, concave).
Formation of images by lenses (real, virtual, magnified, reduced).
Lens equation (qualitative discussion).
subtopics.importance: Practical application of refraction and image formation.

subtopics.name: Optical Instruments
keyPoints: Human eye and its limitations.
Microscopes and telescopes (basic principles).
subtopics.importance: Connects optics to real-world applications and instruments.

topics.importance: Core of the optics curriculum, building on wave properties and introducing practical applications.

topics.topicName: Wave-Particle Duality & Light as a Quantum Phenomenon
keyPoints: Photoelectric effect (qualitative explanation – energy of photons).
Compton scattering (brief overview).
Connecting photon energy to the electromagnetic spectrum (higher frequency = higher energy).
topics.importance: Introduces the quantum nature of light and reinforces the wave-particle duality.

keyPoints: Light as an electromagnetic wave – relationship to electric and magnetic fields.
Preview of electric charge and fields (qualitative connection to light emission).
Brief discussion of how circuits can generate electromagnetic radiation (e.g., antennas).
topics.importance: Provides a bridge to the upcoming electrostatics and circuits unit.

finalNotes: This curriculum emphasizes conceptual understanding and connections between topics. Mathematical derivations should be minimized to focus on the underlying principles.
